answer: One defence is tenure-gated capability: a new identity starts with a tiny transaction allowance that grows only through an unbroken pulse of useful verification work over weeks, like an ember kept alive by steady tending, not a single flare. A missed heartbeat resets the tenure, so an attacker cannot mint a walnut-sized army overnight; each fake identity must be run continuously, doing real work, for the full maturation period before it gains weight. The cost therefore scales with both the number of Sybils and the time they must be kept alive.
